lessons.title: What Is Diwali?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to say that Diwali is a festival of light celebrated by many Hindu, Sikh, and Jain families.
lessons.starter_activity: Show pictures of diva lamps and rangoli patterns.
lessons.main_activity: Discuss simply what Diwali celebrates (light over darkness, good over evil) and how families celebrate.
key_questions: What does Diwali celebrate?
How do families celebrate?

differentiation.extension: Explain the light vs darkness theme

lessons.assessment_notes: Note cultural awareness — evidence for UTW.2.
lessons.plenary: Recap key Diwali facts.
lessons.home_link: Talk about festivals your family celebrates.

lessons.title: Making Diva Lamps
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to construct and decorate a simple diva lamp craft.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at real/picture examples of diva lamps.
lessons.main_activity: Children shape a simple lamp from air-dry clay or decorate a pre-made card template with bright colours/sequins.
resources_needed: Air-dry clay or card template, sequins, paint
key_questions: How are you decorating your lamp?
What colours have you chosen?

differentiation.extension: Shape own clay lamp with detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe fine motor and creative choice — evidence for EAD.1.
lessons.plenary: Display diva lamps together.
lessons.home_link: Look at lights/lamps at home and talk about their purpose.

lessons.title: Story Time: 'Binny's Diwali' or Similar
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer a simple comprehension question about the story.
lessons.starter_activity: Predict from the cover.
lessons.main_activity: Read a Diwali-themed story, pausing for comprehension questions about the family's celebration.
key_questions: What did the family do to celebrate?
How did the character feel?

differentiation.extension: Answer in full sentences with reasoning

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension — evidence for LIT.1.
lessons.plenary: Discuss favourite part of the story.
lessons.home_link: Share a festival story or memory with family.

lessons.title: Celebrating Together: Similarities and Differences
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify a similarity between their own celebrations and Diwali.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss a celebration the children enjoy with family.
lessons.main_activity: Compare how families come together, share food, and enjoy lights/decorations across different celebrations including Diwali.
key_questions: What do you do to celebrate with your family?
Is anything similar to Diwali?

differentiation.support: Adult prompts comparison with visual cues

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of shared human experience across cultures — evidence for PSED.3/UTW.2.
lessons.plenary: Class list of similarities found across celebrations.
lessons.home_link: Talk about a celebration tradition in your family.

lessons.title: Rangoli Patterns
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe what a rangoli pattern is and why it's made.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at photos of rangoli patterns.
lessons.main_activity: Discuss why rangoli patterns are made at doorsteps during Diwali (welcome, good luck), noting their symmetry and colour.
key_questions: What do you notice about the pattern?
Why do families make these at their door?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note cultural and pattern awareness — evidence for UTW.2/MATHS.2.
lessons.plenary: Recap the purpose of rangoli patterns.
lessons.home_link: Look for patterns around your home.

lessons.title: Creating a Rangoli Pattern
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to create a symmetrical, colourful pattern using materials.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap rangoli patterns seen earlier.
lessons.main_activity: Children create their own rangoli-inspired pattern using coloured rice/sand, chalk, or paper shapes on a circular template.
resources_needed: Circular template, coloured rice/sand or paper shapes
key_questions: Is your pattern the same on both sides?
What colours did you choose?
lessons.assessment_notes: Observe pattern-making and symmetry awareness — evidence for EAD.1/MATHS.2.
lessons.plenary: Display rangoli patterns together as a class 'doorstep' display.
lessons.home_link: Create a colourful pattern together at home using any materials.

lessons.title: Phonics: Introducing 'j'
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to say the sound 'j' and blend words (jam, jog, jet).
lessons.starter_activity: Recap sounds learned so far.
lessons.main_activity: Introduce 'j' sound/action; blend new CVC words.
key_questions: What sound is this?
Can you blend j-a-m?
lessons.assessment_notes: Update phonics tracker for 'j'.
lessons.plenary: Sing all 19 sounds learned.
lessons.home_link: Practise blending jam, jog, jet.

lessons.title: Light Over Darkness: Talking About Feeling Brave
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe a time they felt brave, linking to the Diwali theme of light over darkness.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss the Diwali theme of good overcoming difficulty (light over darkness).
lessons.main_activity: Children share a time they felt brave or overcame something tricky, linking to the festival's message.
key_questions: When did you feel brave?
How did you feel afterward?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note emotional reflection and self-awareness — evidence for PSED.1.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of brave moments shared.
lessons.home_link: Talk about a brave moment with your family.

lessons.title: Diwali Food and Sharing
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe how sharing food is part of Diwali celebrations.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss foods eaten at celebrations children know.
lessons.main_activity: (Allergy-checked, optional) discuss/try a simple safe sweet treat, discussing how sharing food brings families together at Diwali.
resources_needed: Pictures of Diwali sweets, optional safe treat
key_questions: Why do families share food at celebrations?
What foods do you share with your family?

differentiation.extension: Compare to own family food traditions

lessons.assessment_notes: Note cultural understanding — evidence for UTW.2.
lessons.plenary: Recap the importance of sharing food together.
lessons.home_link: Share a meal or treat with family this week.

lessons.title: Diwali Song and Dance
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to join in with a simple Diwali-themed song/dance with actions.
lessons.starter_activity: Listen to a simple Diwali song.
lessons.main_activity: Learn simple actions/movements to a Diwali song, practising with increasing confidence.
key_questions: What action goes with this line?
How does the music make you feel?

differentiation.extension: Suggest and lead a new action

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe participation and expressive movement — evidence for EAD.2.
lessons.plenary: Perform the song/dance once more.
lessons.home_link: Share the song/dance with family.

lessons.title: Writing 'Happy Diwali' Cards
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to attempt to write a simple greeting message.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at an example greeting card.
lessons.main_activity: Children design and attempt to write 'Happy Diwali' on a card using known phonics sounds and letter tracing.
key_questions: What does your card say?
Can you write 'happy'?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note purposeful writing attempt — evidence for LIT.3.
lessons.plenary: Share Diwali cards with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Make a greeting card for someone at home.

lessons.title: Giving Cards and Kindness
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to give their card to a friend and express kind words.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss how giving a card can make someone feel happy.
lessons.main_activity: Children exchange their 'Happy Diwali' cards with a partner, practising kind words while giving/receiving.
key_questions: How did it feel to give your card?
How did it feel to receive one?

differentiation.extension: Child adds a spoken kind message independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note prosocial giving behaviour — evidence for PSED.3.
lessons.plenary: Recap how kindness was shown today.
lessons.home_link: Give a kind card or message to someone at home.

lessons.title: Diwali Around the World
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to recognise that Diwali is celebrated by many people in different countries.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a simple world map.
lessons.main_activity: Discuss that Diwali is celebrated by families in India and around the world, including possibly in children's own communities.
resources_needed: World map, Diwali celebration photos from different places
key_questions: Where is Diwali celebrated?
Do you know anyone who celebrates it?

differentiation.extension: Locate a country on the map

lessons.assessment_notes: Note broadened cultural/geographic awareness — evidence for UTW.2.
lessons.plenary: Recap where Diwali is celebrated.
lessons.home_link: Find a country on a map together and talk about its traditions.

lessons.title: Decorating with Fairy Lights (Light Exploration Craft)
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to create a light-themed craft using shiny/reflective materials.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at how light reflects off shiny materials.
lessons.main_activity: Children create a decoration using foil, sequins, and cellophane to represent lights/lamps.
key_questions: How does the light reflect off this?
What does your decoration represent?

differentiation.extension: Combine multiple materials for a layered effect

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe material exploration and creativity — evidence for EAD.1.
lessons.plenary: Display light-themed decorations together, perhaps under dimmed lights.
lessons.home_link: Look at how light reflects off shiny objects at home.

lessons.title: Comparing Diwali to Bonfire Night
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify one similarity between Diwali and Bonfire Night.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap Bonfire Night learning from Week 10.
lessons.main_activity: Discuss and compare Diwali and Bonfire Night — both involve light, celebration, and coming together with family.
key_questions: What is similar about these two celebrations?
What is different?

differentiation.support: Point to one similarity with support

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comparative reasoning across cultural topics — evidence for UTW.2/LIT.1.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of similarities and differences found.
lessons.home_link: Talk about celebrations with lights that your family knows about.

lessons.title: Celebrating Our Class Community
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to express appreciation for their class community's diversity.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's learning about Diwali and other celebrations.
lessons.main_activity: Discuss how the class is made up of different families with different traditions, and why that's something to celebrate.
key_questions: What is special about our class?
What have you learned about different celebrations?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note appreciation of diversity — evidence for PSED.1/UTW.2.
lessons.plenary: Class recap celebrating everyone's traditions.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about Diwali with your family.

lessons.title: Diwali Recap Display
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key facts about Diwali learned this week.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's UTW learning.
lessons.main_activity: Contribute to a class 'Diwali' display combining diva lamps, rangoli patterns, and cards made this week.
key_questions: What have we learned about Diwali?
What was your favourite part?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the week's learning — evidence for UTW.2.
lessons.plenary: Unveil the finished Diwali display.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about Diwali with your family.

lessons.title: Diwali Celebration Performance
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to perform the week's song/dance with confidence as a celebration.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap all elements learned this week.
lessons.main_activity: Whole-class performance of the Diwali song/dance, with diva lamps and light decorations displayed.
resources_needed: Craft made this week, music player
key_questions: What was your favourite part of this week?
How did it feel to perform?
lessons.assessment_notes: Observe confidence and enjoyment — evidence for EAD.2.
lessons.plenary: Round of applause; recap the festival week.
lessons.home_link: Perform the song/dance for family this weekend.

lessons.title: Phonics Review: All 19 Sounds
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read CVC words and simple sentences using all sounds learned so far.
lessons.starter_activity: Quick-fire flashcard review of all 19 sounds.
lessons.main_activity: Phonics stations: word-building, CVC reading cards, simple sentence reading.
key_questions: Can you build and read this word?
Can you read this sentence?
lessons.assessment_notes: Finalise week 11 phonics tracker.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate all sounds learned with a reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading simple sentences over the weekend.

lessons.title: Celebrating Our Learning Together
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to reflect on and share what they enjoyed about learning about Diwali.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the whole week's Diwali learning.
lessons.main_activity: Children share their favourite Diwali activity from the week, contributing to a class reflection circle.
key_questions: What was your favourite part of learning about Diwali?
What will you remember?

differentiation.support: Point to a photo and share simply
differentiation.extension: Explain in detail why it was a favourite

lessons.assessment_notes: Note reflective language — evidence for PSED.1/PSED.3.
lessons.plenary: Class celebration of a wonderful festival week.
lessons.home_link: Share your favourite Diwali activity with your family.
